open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M12 — StoreHistory
open_points.text:
A restored store therefore holds this record exactly as the backup
holds it — the backup's last sequence number, and its migration closure when
the backup was made after the import, none when it was made before — and
Registry neither knows nor records that the store was restored.

Registry makes it, with no closure and number 0, in the transaction that
makes a new, empty store (State 2 A17 rule 5); it never makes a second one.

That store begins its own history from the
backup: every change after it is lost, the audit entries with it, and
Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within
each store's history;
open_points.question: Does restoring a backup continue the backed-up StoreHistory entity, or begin a new StoreHistory entity for the restored store; if it begins a new entity, who mints it and from which backed-up facts?
options: The backed-up StoreHistory entity continues unchanged.
The owner mints a new StoreHistory entity when placing the backup, using the backup's facts.
Registry mints a new StoreHistory entity when it starts on the restored store, using the backup's facts.
open_points.default_guess: Treat restoration as beginning a new StoreHistory entity, minted outside Registry by the owner's backup replacement from the backed-up facts, because R0-89 says the restored store begins its own history and Registry cannot know that restoration occurred.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M12 — StoreHistory facts
open_points.question: Replace these prose-only facts with explicit field declarations that name every field and state its type, including the migration closure's absence or optionality.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M12 — StoreHistory composition
open_points.text:
The two facts change for different reasons — every audit append, and the
one import — but they are kept in one record because they share one scope
and one life, the store's history (R0-89), and no caller reads either apart
from the store it is in. Each is changed only by its own transaction, and
neither changes the other.
open_points.rule: Не смешивай таблицы только потому, что у них похожая форма. Решение о merge/split принимается по change-axis: что меняется вместе и по одной причине.
open_points.question: Make the model boundary follow the change-axis: either split the independently changed facts or establish that they change together for one reason.
